analysis:
No finding qualifies from the visible text. The workflow was supplied as head text only, with no base or patch, so I could not tell which release-swift.yml lines changed. identity-binding.md (0f28dd130f856b2e:0) was supplied as metadata only, and the Swift and script sources behind the claims were not supplied.

release-swift.yml (head), lines 591-1258:
- Signing re-signs the CLI with entitlements built by prepare-app-attest-entitlements.py, then asserts aps-environment=production, get-task-allow absent, keychain-access-groups, and the hard-coded access group SLDQ2GJ6TL.io.darkbloom.provider (638-648, 664-686).
- The fan helper is checked against a designated requirement tied to the team OU (593-596, 847-849).
- A post-notarization step verifies the staple, cmp of flat and app binaries, and the final tar layout. It extracts the tar, runs runtime-smoke, and derives BINARY_HASH, CODE_DIRECTORY_HASH (full SHA-256 CDHash) and the SDK version from the final extracted bytes (798-903). This supports T-054, T-034 and A-017.
- Publication is split into three jobs: build-and-release signs and uploads the publication artifact; stage-release downloads it by artifact id and digest and stages it to R2; publish-release registers it with the coordinator using the release key (A-005) and moves aliases. The download is pinned by artifact id, digest and signing run id (1062-1073, 1170-1181). Publish is serialized by a concurrency group (1096).
- Validation-only runs retain a signed bundle for 14 days and run it on older macOS. That lane's identity JSON comes from the same artifact as the bundle, so its hash check proves integrity only against accidental change (1220-1258).

Supply-chain point the next pass should check: stage-release and publish-release export R2 keys and the release key to GITHUB_ENV before the unpinned `pip install awscli` (1074-1079, 1182-1187). If this is new in the PR rather than pre-existing, it exposes A-005 and A-011 to compromise of the awscli package or its dependencies; the fix is to pin it by hash or install it before secrets are exported. I did not confirm whether the lines are new.

encryption.md (a863bda6ca614785:1-3) adds a claim at head line 108 that dev builds use a separate KEK and Secure Enclave key (keychain prefix io.darkbloom.dev), so the dev and production caches are isolated. That claim is not verifiable from the supplied files. T-041 and TB-003 do not model a dev and a production provider coexisting on one Mac, with separate tokens (A-008), ports and attestation identities. The changelog (e56f05f8b76b625b) says dev and production can run on the same Mac and use different keychain items and paths.

The next pass should check the Swift keychain-prefix, path and port derivation, the installer's `-dev.` selection logic, and whether the dev identity can register against the production coordinator.
